blogs.title: What the 2019 Rakhigarhi genome study reports
blogs.excerpt: The published analysis reports genome-wide data from one individual, I6113, excavated at Rakhigarhi. See reference [1].
blogs.content: The study reports one ancient genome from Rakhigarhi and discusses ancestry using its stated comparative framework. A single ancient individual cannot by itself establish linguistic continuity or represent every Harappan population. Read the original paper for methods, limitations, and conclusions.

blogs.title: Rakhigarhi site overview: use source-specific measurements
blogs.excerpt: Official and scholarly sources describe the site’s mounds and extent using different figures; cite the specific source and definition used.
blogs.content: The Archaeological Survey of India describes seven mounds. Government and scholarly sources report different area estimates depending on what is counted. This prototype therefore avoids presenting one area figure as a settled measurement. See references [2] and [3].

blogs.title: How to publish digital heritage models responsibly
blogs.excerpt: A synthetic model should never be mistaken for a measured artifact or excavation record.
blogs.content: This prototype uses procedural geometry solely to demonstrate a viewer. It contains no scans, museum objects, excavation models, or verified mound coordinates. Replace the models only with assets that have documented provenance, permissions, and descriptive metadata.

literature.title: Rakhigarhi: evidence and limits
literature.intro: This page summarizes cited public sources. The proposed Rakhigarhi Research Foundation is a concept in this prototype; this site does not claim it is an established institution.

sections.heading: Site and mounds
sections.text: Government sources describe Rakhigarhi in Haryana as a major Harappan site and identify seven mounds. Published area figures vary by source and by what boundary is being measured, so this prototype does not present a single total area as definitive.

sections.heading: The 2019 genome paper
sections.text: The paper reports genome-wide data from one individual, I6113, from Rakhigarhi. Its findings are specific to that sample and the authors’ analysis; they do not establish linguistic continuity or stand for every person in the Indus Civilization. Read the study’s methods and limitations before drawing broader conclusions.

sections.heading: Reservoir reporting
sections.text: A December 2024 news report describes evidence of a water-storage area between Mounds 1 and 2 and quotes an ASI official on an estimated depth of 3.5–4 feet. This prototype does not call it a monumental reservoir at RGR-3; consult the primary excavation report for definitive interpretation.

references.text: Shinde et al. (2019), “An Ancient Harappan Genome Lacks Ancestry from Steppe Pastoralists or Iranian Farmers,” Cell 179(3):729–735.e10.
